registry_info.name: instruction_bench
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `tell` family (7 registry names, 3 declaration orders, one shared set of four values). One chair assembly, part-way built, standing in four bays at once, so the four theories of instruction can be compared instead of chosen between.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The `tell` word and its four values are PRELOADED from furniture_assembly_puzzle.gd at runtime and checked in both directions at _ready, and so is the chair plan itself; do not retype either here or in the script. The two axes declared below are NOT that word - see dna.declines.

instruction_bench.name: Instruction Bench
instruction_bench.description: One chair assembly, part-way built, standing four times on a single deck and told four different ways: under a translucent ghost of everything still to come, under nothing at all, under kerbs and stakes that give position and withhold form, and beside a finished chair in solid wood. The plan is the family's own chair - read live out of FurnitureAssemblyPuzzle's _setup_chair_targets at build time, never transcribed - and the work already standing is identical in all four bays, so the only thing that differs between them is what is said about the rest. `built` changes how much of the assembly is standing when the telling is given: a seat alone, a seat on one leg, a seat on both front legs, or a seat on all four with only the back left. `slip` changes which of the three transformations the standing work gets wrong - none, a tilt, a displacement, or one rung down the family's own scale ladder - each derived from the chair's own tolerances. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random: one plan read once and drawn six ways.
interactions: walk the four bays and find the one whose telling never changes when the work does
set built=stood and watch four theories of instruction shrink to four ways of pointing at one missing back
set built=plane and see the same four bays at their furthest apart, when nothing has been done and everything must be said
set slip=place and ask which of the four bays lets you know the seat is wrong
notice that the exemplar bay is the only one that needs floor space of its own, and ask what that costs
instruction_bench.qfep_connection: Four theories of how a person comes to know how to make something, standing at once so that none of them can pass as the natural one. The bench cannot exempt itself: presenting four tellings in a row on a common deck with nothing to say which is which is itself the `none` claim, the one that says the work should speak for itself, and the artifact states that rather than pretending to a view from nowhere. What the axes then show is that instruction is not a quantity to be dosed. Three of the four tellings are about YOUR chair and shrink as you build it; the fourth is a finished chair that has never heard of you and is exactly the same size whether you have done one piece or five. And when the work is wrong, the silent bay is silent in a second way, because there is nothing beside it for the error to be an error against.
instruction_bench.relationships: synthesis over the `tell` family (assembly_line_puzzle, chair_/shelf_/stool_/table_assembly_puzzle, balance_puzzle, configurable_portal); adopts its word by exhibiting it rather than sweeping it, as taxonomy_hall does with `taxonomy`; reads both its four words and its chair plan live out of furniture_assembly_puzzle.gd

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The deck is 3.12 m across the four bays by 0.56 m deep, so a 4 x 1 clear strip with room to stand in front of it. Every bay reads from +Z and the exemplar's extra chair extends the row to the +X end, so the artifact wants approaching from +Z with the ghost bay on the left; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you get that. There is no collider anywhere in the file - the pathfinder will route straight through the chairs, which is correct, because there are no chairs, there are four pictures of one.

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants and the family's own chair targets, re-derived in a Python replica of the geometry and rasterised at the sweep camera; no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts, and every drawn node in this artifact is a MeshInstance3D holding a BoxMesh. X: four bays at 0.64 pitch run -0.96..+0.96 before the recentring shift, the exemplar's finished chair stands +0.60 beyond the last bay at +1.56, and the deck adds a 0.20 chair half-width plus 0.10 of margin at each end, giving -1.26..+1.86 = 3.12 m wide about a centre at +0.30 - which ORIGIN_SHIFT = -0.30 moves onto the artifact's own origin, so the deck runs -1.56..+1.56. Y from 0 (the deck underside, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed) to 0.934, the top of the ghost shell over the chair back: deck 0.06 plus the back target's 0.67 centre plus half of 0.40 x 1.02. The solid back tops out at 0.930 and the seat at slip=turn reaches only 0.610, so that shell is the tallest thing on the bench in every tile that has one. Z -0.28..+0.28 is the deck, 0.076 m clear of the deepest thing standing on it (a ghost shell at 0.204). The box is IDENTICAL at every value of both axes except for that shell, which is absent only where nothing remains to be ghosted; so the camera does not move between tiles for any reason other than the sweep's own union pre-pass.

dna.axis_shape: `built` NESTS - its four values are prefixes of ONE build order, so the set of standing pieces at each value contains the set at the value below it (plane 1 in prop 2 in pair 3 in stood 5). That order is not invented: it is the order furniture_assembly_puzzle.gd::_setup_chair_targets() appends its six targets in, and instruction_bench.gd reads that array at build time rather than retyping it. `slip` sits SIDE BY SIDE - translate, rotate and scale are the three generators the family's own identity block names as sufficient, no one of them contains another, and `sound` is their common zero. Both are named because they call for opposite handling under trimming: dropping the tail of a nested axis only lowers the ceiling, dropping the tail of a parallel one loses a case.
dna.default:
built=prop, slip=sound. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of PLACED artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the loudest or the emptiest.

WHY `prop` AND NOT `plane` OR `stood`. `stood` is the weakest default: with five of six pieces standing, one target remains, so every bay draws exactly one telling and four theories of instruction shrink to four ways of pointing at the same missing back. That convergence is the axis's whole finding and it is worth a tile, not the tile a visitor meets first. `plane` is the loudest and the least honest: a seat floating on nothing is barely an assembly under way, and with five targets outstanding the bench photographs as four diagrams rather than as four commentaries on a piece of work - it is also the value at which `none` is most obviously useless, which stacks the argument before the visitor has asked the question. `prop` is a plane resting on a single column: unmistakably part-built, unmistakably not finished, four targets still to tell, and one of them - the front-right leg - standing clear of the seat where every bay can draw it unoccluded. Measured, `prop` is also the value whose telling areas sit nearest the middle of the range: ghost 5,696 px against a 3,451-6,668 span, mark 1,789 px against 970-2,158.

WHY `sound`. The slip axis asks whether a telling can catch a mistake, and that is only legible against a frame in which there is no mistake. A default that already carried one would make a visitor's first reading of the bench a reading of a wrong chair.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the seven `tell` declarations leave unbuilt: every member's own note describes the four values as four ways of disclosing one plan, and not one of them can stand two of those disclosures at the same time, because a puzzle can only be told one way at once. Six of the seven also hand their telling to an UNTOUCHED puzzle - the guides are built in _ready before a single piece has moved - so the family has never once photographed a telling given to work already under way.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHY IT NEEDS A BENCH RATHER THAN A MEMBER.

The family's four words are four theories of how someone learns to assemble a thing. `none` tells you nothing and you work it out. `mark` gives you where and withholds what. `ghost` gives you the finished thing as a translucent preview, so you are filling in an outline somebody else drew. `exemplar` stands a completed one beside you, which is the only value where you are copying rather than solving. Seven registry names declare the word and every one of them STANDS IN one telling and forgoes the other three, so none of them can put the ghost next to the silence for the same chair, and none of them can show that the four are different KINDS of instruction rather than four amounts of one.

So the bench reads the chair plan ONCE - out of the family's own _setup_chair_targets(), never transcribed - and stands it four times on one deck in the family's own order. What varies instead is the second decision every telling makes and the family never varies: HOW MUCH OF THE WORK IS ALREADY DONE when the telling is given, and whether that work is right.

WHAT IT FOUND, all of it computed in Python before anything was built.

(1) THE TELLINGS CONVERGE AS THE WORK PROCEEDS, AND ONE OF THEM DOES NOT. Drawn alone at the capture camera, the ghost bay's telling covers 6,668 px at built=plane, 5,696 at prop, 5,279 at pair and 3,451 at stood - it loses 48% of itself as the work goes from one standing piece to five. The mark bay's telling runs 2,158 / 1,789 / 1,514 / 970, losing 55%. `none` is 0 at every value by definition. THE EXEMPLAR IS 9,302 px AT EVERY VALUE, IDENTICAL TO THE PIXEL. It is simultaneously the largest telling on the bench and the only one blind to how far you have got, because it is not about your chair at all - it is a second, finished chair. Three of the four tellings track your progress and shrink; the fourth is a rival object that does not know you exist.

(2) THE OBJECT IS ITSELF AN INSTRUCTION, WHICH IS WHY THE AXIS EXISTS. At built=stood the chair stands on four legs and only the back is missing; the shape of what is left is legible from the work without any telling at all, which is exactly why the four bays are closest there. The `none` bay is not a control for nothing - it is the reading that says the work is the only instruction, and the axis measures what that reading costs at each stage.

(3) A TELLING IS ALSO A CHECK, AND `none` CANNOT PERFORM IT. `slip` displaces, tilts or shrinks the seat by an amount the family's own tolerances call a failure. The wrong seat appears identically in all four bays - it is the same standing work - but only three of the four put anything beside it for it to be wrong AGAINST. This is the one claim on the bench that a pixel count cannot make for you: the change is equal everywhere and the meaning is not, and dna.still_note says so in advance rather than after a number arrives.

(4) THE FAMILY QUANTISES ONE TRANSFORMATION AND NOT THE OTHER TWO, which is why the three slips are not derived the same way. position_tolerance and rotation_tolerance are rulers over continuous quantities, so `place` and `turn` are 1.5x them (0.08 -> 0.12 m, 15 -> 22.5 degrees), read off the target itself. Scale is not continuous: grab_cube_scalable.gd snaps it to [0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0] times a 0.1 m base, so the smallest scale error a player can physically commit is ONE RUNG - for the seat's 0.40 (the 4.0 rung) that is 0.30, a 0.10 m error which is 3.33x the 0.03 scale_tolerance. There is no near miss available in scale. The asymmetry is a fact about the family, not a liberty taken here.

(5) THE GHOST'S EDGE HAS NEVER BEEN AN EDGE. transform_puzzle_base.gd::_create_ghost_for_target builds a second box at target_scale * 1.02 with CULL_FRONT and calls it an 'edge wireframe effect'. 1.02 of a 0.05 m leg is a 0.25 mm shell: 0.08 px at this bench's 201.7 px/m, and under a fifth of a pixel even at the family's own single-chair framing. What it contributes is a second translucent layer - more alpha, not an outline. The bench builds it exactly as the family builds it and does not correct it, because the bench exists to show the family's ghost and not an improved one.
dna.kin:
THE WORD IS TAKEN WHOLE AND NOT RETYPED. instruction_bench.gd opens with
const FAM := preload("res://commons/primitives/furniture/furniture_assembly_puzzle.gd")
and the bays, their number and their order come from FAM's own TELLS at build time, read as FAM.TELLS rather than through Object.get() (a const is not a property, so get() would return null and the bench would fall back silently to its own copy) and rather than through get_script_constant_map() (non-static, cannot be called on the class at all). FAM.TELLS also fails at PARSE time if the const ever disappears, which is a better failure mode than either. _check_family_list() runs at _ready and push_errors in BOTH directions: a value the family declares that this bench has no bay for, and a bay this bench builds that the family has dropped.

THE PLAN IS ALSO READ AND NOT RETYPED, which is the part that could most easily have drifted. _family_plan() constructs FAM.new() OFF THE TREE - so _ready never runs, no ghosts are built, no pieces are spawned, no tween is created and no piece_scene is needed - calls _setup_furniture_targets(), copies the six PieceTargets out as plain Dictionaries and frees the probe. Positions, rotations, sizes AND the three tolerances the slip axis is derived from all come from there. If the chair plan changes, this bench changes with it and cannot photograph a chair the family no longer builds.

ONE THING IS TRANSCRIBED, ON THE RECORD. The scale ladder [0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0] and its 0.1 m base live on an @export and a plain var in grab_cube_scalable.gd (lines 17 and 58), whose base class is XRToolsPickable. Preloading it would drag the XR addon into the parse chain of a bench that has no business needing one, and a promotion has already been lost in this corpus to code that lived inside a gitignored addon. So the ladder is copied with the citation rather than read, and it is the only number in this file that is.

THE ORDER THIS BENCH TOOK, AND THE TWO IT DID NOT. All seven members carry the SAME FOUR VALUES; the split is PURE REORDERING, and each order hoists that member's own default to the front. Five declare ghost | none | mark | exemplar (assembly_line_puzzle, chair_/shelf_/stool_/table_assembly_puzzle); balance_puzzle declares mark | none | ghost | exemplar; configurable_portal declares mark | ghost | exemplar | none. This bench takes the five-member order, because those five are assembly puzzles and this is a bench of an assembly, and because chair_assembly_puzzle is the scene the plan is read out of.

WHAT THE THREE ORDERS ACTUALLY COST, in arithmetic, because build_dna_gallery trims from the TAIL. A capped single-axis `tell` sweep drops exemplar-then-mark under the assembly order, exemplar-then-ghost under the balance order, and none-then-exemplar under the portal order. At cap 3 the assembly and balance orders are measured on the SAME SET {ghost, none, mark} and differ only in tile order, while the portal is measured on {mark, ghost, exemplar} - two of three in common. At cap 2 the three sets are {ghost, none}, {mark, none} and {mark, ghost}, pairwise sharing exactly ONE value out of two. So `tell` at --max 3 or above compares like with like for six of the seven, and below that nothing about that family is comparable. Three orders mean three different values get dropped first; this is the threshold at which that stops mattering.

THE PALETTE IS THE FAMILY'S, member by member. Ghost fill and shell: transform_puzzle_base.gd's ghost_color Color(0.0, 0.8, 1.0), ghost_alpha 0.25 (fill at alpha * 0.5, shell at alpha), ghost_emission_energy 0.8 (fill at energy * 0.3, shell at energy), both SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED, fill CULL_DISABLED and shell CULL_FRONT - the same six numbers and the same two cull modes. Mark: furniture_assembly_puzzle.gd::_tell_mark's lit material is ghost_color at alpha 1.0 with emission_energy * 1.6, and its stem is Color(0.10, 0.12, 0.15) at roughness 0.85; both taken exactly. Deck: balance_puzzle.gd's platform_color Color(0.30, 0.30, 0.35).

ONE SUBSTITUTION, AND IT IS NOT A DRIFT. The family's solid pieces use res://commons/resourses/shaders/wood.gdshader with light_color (0.952941, 0.858824, 0.74902) and dark_color (0.74902, 0.619608, 0.490196). This bench draws their arithmetic mean, Color(0.85098, 0.739216, 0.619608), as a flat StandardMaterial3D. The reason is a standing measured fact in this project: headless Godot never reimports, so a shader edit does not reach the sweep and a stale compiled shader photographs as a dead axis - gyroid_demo read 0.00% on both of its axes across sixteen byte-identical tiles for exactly that reason. A grain that cannot be trusted to be the same grain in every tile is worse than no grain, and a synthesis whose whole subject is a comparison cannot afford one.
dna.declines:
`tell` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S VARYING AXIS, on the record, and the refusal is the design.

THE CASE IS MIXED, and it was read out of the members' CODE rather than their prose. In furniture_assembly_puzzle.gd::_setup_ghost_guides() the word is spent in one `match tell:` whose arms are `pass` / _tell_mark() / _tell_exemplar() / super(), preceded by _clear_tell_nodes() so values cannot stack; balance_puzzle.gd::_rebuild_tell() and configurable_portal.gd are the same switch. assembly_line_puzzle.gd::_apply_tell() makes the mixture explicit because all four arms act on ONE mesh_instance: "none" sets layers = 0 and therefore SUBTRACTS the default; "mark" swaps the mesh for a small bright head; "exemplar" swaps the material for an opaque one; ghost falls through untouched. One subtraction and two parallel substitutions.

So the DISCLOSURE partially nests where the APPARATUS does not. none's information is contained in mark's, and mark's in ghost's - _tell_mark draws its footprint from target_scale.x and .z and puts a head at the target point, so it gives plan position and plan footprint and withholds height extent and orientation, all of which the ghost box gives. But not one node of the mark is a node of the ghost, and `exemplar` is not the top of that ladder at all: it discloses the same targets as ghost in a different modality, as a finished rival object rather than an outline to fill. A parallel set cannot be swept without demolishing three quarters of the exhibit, and the large number that would produce would be a measurement of the bench being dismantled.

`fault` IS REFUSED AS A NAME for the second axis. impossible_trident already declares fault: global | confessed | none | doubled, which asks where the contradiction in an impossible figure LIVES. Same word, different question, incompatible values - and a second `fault` with a different value list is exactly the ambiguity that makes two tools disagree about the same tokens, which is the tell this corpus keeps rediscovering. `slip` is unused across all 465 declared axis names; so is `built`.

TIME IS REFUSED, and it is the interesting decline. The strongest unbuilt axis on this family is WHEN the telling is given and whether it survives being used - a ghost that clears as you fill it, a mark that appears only after you go wrong, an exemplar taken away once you have looked. Every value of it is a fact about a sequence and the evidence here is ONE STILL PNG per value, so a still would photograph the shutter and not the axis. info_board was swept across five duration exports and produced six identical tiles; this is the same shape of mistake, and it is declined rather than shipped as a finished-looking experiment.

THE GHOST'S EDGE IS NOT FIXED, deliberately. The 1.02 shell is 0.08 px at this framing and draws no outline; giving it a real thickness in metres would make the bench's ghost more legible AND make it a different object from the ghost the family actually ships, which is the one thing a synthesis may not do. Recorded in dna.note (5) instead, with the arithmetic.

TEXT IS DECLINED, and here it is the family's decision rather than a legibility limit. The assembly puzzles are explicitly textless - success_message defaults to "" and show_success_label to false, and the docstring says "Clean Alyx-style completion - pieces snap with satisfying pulse, no text". A captioned bench would be a different object from the thing it exhibits, and a bay is identified by what it draws, which is the entire point of the word. There is not one Label3D and not one glyph in any tile.

THE BENCH CANNOT EXEMPT ITSELF, and does not pretend to. Four bays standing in a row on a common deck with nothing to say which is which is the `none` register: the bench tells you nothing about its own four tellings and leaves you to work them out. That is a position, it is the position this artifact takes, and it is stated here rather than hidden.
dna.measured: MEASURED 2026-08-13, all sixteen frames. THE EQUALITY IT PREDICTED HELD, AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE INSIDE ITS OWN TOLERANCE. It claimed the six `slip` pairs must read nearly the same in every `built` context, because the slipped piece is the seat and the seat stands at every value of `built`, and set 2.0 points as the threshold above which the axes would be entangled. Worst spread measured: 0.19 points. Every slip pair is flat across contexts — sound vs size 1.19/1.22/1.23/1.28, turn vs place 2.43/2.49/2.53/2.61. A structural claim about axis INDEPENDENCE, verified from the same sweep, and far harder to satisfy by accident than a percentage. THE FRAME-CURRENCY AXIS MEAN ALSO HELD: predicted `built` 0.963% of frame, measured 0.79-1.08% across its six pairs. THE SPECIFIC PAIR WAS WRONG: it named prop against plane, which measures 0.96-1.08%; the floor is stood against pair at 0.79%, at slip = place. Off by one place in a band five hundredths wide. Left alone — an axis whose weakest pair is 0.79% and whose structure verified exactly is not a repair target.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency and not in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own corner background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5% (1,280 samples). Every number below comes from rasterising this exact geometry at this exact camera (RES 760, FOV 34, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, PAD 1.9, dna.framing 0.60) in Python with a z-buffer, one directional light and back-to-front alpha for the ghosts, then pushing the result through that same pipeline. READ EVERY NUMBER AS A FLOOR: a flat rasteriser has no shadows, no ambient occlusion and no antialiasing, and every prediction in this corpus that named a pair and a number has under-predicted, by 1.5x to 6.7x.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `built` prop <-> plane, IN ALL FOUR SLIP CONTEXTS. Predicted focus 10.04% (sound), 10.40% (place), 10.40% (size), 9.50% (turn) - mean 10.09%, floor 9.50%. THE ARITHMETIC: those two values differ by exactly ONE PIECE, the front-left leg, 0.05 x 0.40 x 0.05 m, whose silhouette from this standpoint is 8.35 x 78.0 px = 651 px. It changes in all four bays at once but in four different ways - solid leg to translucent ghost, solid leg to nothing, solid leg to kerb-and-stake-and-head, solid leg to nothing - which is why 4 x 651 = 2,604 px of leg produces 4,345 changed px. In the crop (555 x 303 = 168,165 px) that is 2.584% of pixels at a mean absolute difference of 97.7 grey levels over the changed ones, i.e. 424,437 grey-levels of change energy; scaled into the critic's 25,600 samples that is 64,613, and the hottest 1,280 carry 1,280 x 0.1004 x 255 = 32,764 of it, i.e. 51%, the rest lost to the 3.5x downsample smearing an 8-px-wide leg across partial samples. If the measured focus comes back near 20% the downsample is not smearing the way the replica says; if it comes back near 2% the fourth bay is not drawing.

THE CLOSEST PAIR ON THE SECOND AXIS IS `slip` sound <-> size, predicted 10.16% mean (9.75% at built=stood, 10.13% pair, 10.28% prop, 10.49% plane), floor 9.75%. NOTE THAT THOSE TWO NUMBERS ARE 0.07 POINTS APART, and that is itself a prediction that can be wrong: the sheet's two weakest pairs are predicted to be a dead heat, one on each axis. If the sweep separates them by more than about two points, one of the two axes is drawing something the replica does not model.

A SECOND PREDICTION, STRONGER BECAUSE IT IS AN EQUALITY. The six `slip` pairs must return NEARLY THE SAME NUMBERS in all four `built` contexts, because the slipped piece is the seat, the seat is the first target in the family's order, and it is therefore standing at every value of `built`. In the replica the spreads across contexts are: sound<->turn 18.77-19.26 (0.49 points), sound<->place 16.02-17.32 (1.30), sound<->size 9.75-10.49 (0.74), turn<->place 18.06-19.21 (1.15), turn<->size 15.40-15.87 (0.47), place<->size 15.88-17.33 (1.45). If any `slip` pair varies by more than about two points across `built`, something other than the seat is reading the slip and the two axes are entangled.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks as though it should be. `slip` place <-> size both make the seat cover less of the deck under it and are the obvious twin candidate on a 16-tile sheet. Predicted 16.92% mean (15.88-17.33): NOT a twin, well clear of the critic's 6% bar. A shift moves 0.12 m of slab to ONE side (20.0 px of travel) while a rung-down removes 0.10 m from BOTH sides (16.7 px each), so the two frames disagree over roughly three times the area either disagrees with `sound` over.

AXIS MEANS PREDICTED, over the 24 same-axis pairs each: `built` frame 0.963% / focus 17.77% -> BITES. `slip` frame 0.843% / focus 16.27% -> BITES. Widest pair on the sheet: `built` stood <-> plane at slip=size, 27.95%. Thinnest pair that is not the closest: `built` stood <-> pair at slip=place, 9.71%.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL SIXTEEN VARIANTS, not from the default. Union 3.12 x 0.934 x 0.56 (x = deck end to deck end across four bays plus the exemplar's own chair; y = deck underside to the top of the chair back's ghost shell; z = deck back to deck front), diagonal sqrt(9.7344 + 0.872356 + 0.3136) = sqrt(10.920356) = 3.30460, radius 1.65230. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 would put the camera at 1.65230 / 0.3057307 x 1.9 = 10.2683 m and show a 6.2787 m frame around a 3.12 m object - PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.60 the camera comes to 6.1610 m and the frame to 3.7672 m, which is 201.74 px per metre. The union's screen-x extent is 3.12 x cos(0.62) + 0.56 x sin(0.62) = 2.5394 + 0.3254 = 2.8647 m, i.e. 76.0% of frame width. Rasterised at that setting and measured across all sixteen tiles, the subject's bounding box runs x 142..697 and y 255..558 - margins of 142 px left, 63 right, 255 top, 202 bottom - and the subject covers 5.85% of the frame at its thinnest tile (plane, turn) and 8.24% at its fullest (stood, place).

THAT IS A SPARSE SUBJECT, NOT A SMALL ONE, and the distinction is taxonomy_hall's. The bounding box spans 73.0% of frame width by construction; four chairs are mostly air, so a pixel count against the background reads low for a correctly framed object. The critic's own blank-render bar is BLANK_SUBJECT = 0.002 and floating_sphere_field is a legitimate artifact at 0.83%. Do not tighten this framing on subject share alone.

TWO OTHER VALUES WERE MEASURED AND REJECTED. 0.58 gives 208.7 px/m and 6.18% subject - better on both counts - but leaves only 51 px of margin on the RIGHT, which is the near end of an obliquely-viewed row and therefore the magnified one; taxonomy_hall rejected 43 px there for the showcase key light's specular fringe, which the replica does not model, and 51 px is not enough more. 0.62 gives 74 px of right margin and drops the thinnest subject tile to 5.42%. 0.60 is the value where the tight margin is 63 px and nothing that carries meaning has fallen under 5 px.

GAUGE CHECK AT 201.74 px/m, because foresight_range shipped a bench's 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane and sorting_hall drew a whole axis three pixels wide. From this standpoint a world displacement projects to screen at 0.8275 of its length along X, 0.9664 along Y and 0.6176 along Z. Leg 0.05 x 0.40 m -> 8.35 x 78.0 px. Seat 0.40 x 0.05 -> 66.8 x 9.8 px. Back plate 0.30 x 0.40 -> 50.1 x 78.0 px. Deck 0.06 thick -> 11.7 px. Stake stem 0.030 -> 5.0 px; stake head 0.048 -> 8.0 px wide, 9.4 px tall. Kerb bar 0.024 thick -> 3.0 px on the runs that lie along X and 4.0 px on the runs that lie along Z, WHICH IS UNDER FIVE, so the bar is given a HEIGHT rather than lying flat as tape: 0.030 m of kerb reads 5.85 px in screen Y, and that is the dimension that separates it from the deck. Making it wider instead was rejected - a leg footprint is 0.05 m, i.e. 8.35 px, and an outline of it drawn in 0.04 m bars is not an outline, it is a blob. Slip magnitudes: place 0.12 m -> 20.0 px of travel; size 0.10 m -> 16.7 px off each of two sides; turn 22.5 degrees on a 0.40 m slab -> the near corner rises 0.0765 m = 14.9 px. Nothing that carries meaning is under 5 px.

THE FAMILY'S OWN MARK NUMBERS DO NOT SURVIVE THIS OBJECT, and that is why they were re-gauged rather than transcribed: _tell_mark's stem is 0.007 m (1.2 px here), its head 0.032 m (5.3 px) and its outline bars 0.008 m (1.3 px). They are sized for a capture of ONE chair filling the frame.

THE ROW RUNS ALONG X AND NOT IN A 2x2, and that was a decision, not a default. A 2 x 2 of bays fills a square frame better and would have raised px/m by roughly a quarter, but the camera pitches only 14.9 degrees down and a chair is 0.87 m tall: a front bay would black out the bottom two thirds of a bay behind it, and the exemplar bay is already two chairs deep in x. A row costs frame area and loses nothing to occlusion.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body, no signal connection and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. _ready is ungated: it reads config metadata, reads the family's word, checks it in both directions and builds the whole bench standalone, so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

THE FAMILY IS PROBED WITHOUT BEING RUN. _family_plan() constructs FurnitureAssemblyPuzzle with .new() and never adds it to the tree, so _ready is not called: no ghost guides are built, no pieces are spawned (auto_spawn_pieces is only read inside _ready), no create_tween() runs, and piece_scene is never dereferenced. _setup_furniture_targets() is a pure function over piece_targets. The probe is freed before _build draws anything. This is the one place the bench touches live family code at runtime and it touches the one method that has no side effects.

DETERMINISM OF THE PLAN ITSELF: _setup_chair_targets() writes six PieceTargets from constant literals, so two boots produce the same six targets on any machine. Two captures of one value are two photographs of one object.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR. The sweep sets the @export properties directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_built / config_slip metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks up to four ancestors for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against _is_built / _is_slip, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once - the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value rather than emptying the bench.

BOTH AXES ARE String ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur. The `slip` axis deliberately does NOT use the word "true" for its zero value, which would have been the natural English and would have arrived from a JSON spec as a boolean.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

THE EXEMPLAR'S OWN CHAIR IS CONSTANT ACROSS BOTH AXES, BY CONSTRUCTION AND ON PURPOSE. It is drawn at the plan and never at the slip - it is the correct answer - and it is complete at every value of `built`. Measured in the replica: the exemplar telling covers 9,302 px at all four values of `built`, identical to the pixel. That is finding (1) in dna.note and it is the bench's sharpest claim, not a dead bay. A future reader who crops to the fourth bay's second chair and reports both axes INERT will have measured the argument and called it a bug. What DOES change in that bay is the partial chair standing beside it.

THE `none` BAY DRAWS NOTHING AT ANY VALUE OF EITHER AXIS except the standing work, which every other bay also draws. Between two `built` values it changes exactly as much as the work does; between two `slip` values it changes exactly as much as the seat does. It is the control, and it is also the position that says the work is the only instruction there is.

THE SLIP IS EQUAL IN ALL FOUR BAYS AND ITS MEANING IS NOT. The wrong seat is the same wrong seat everywhere; what differs is whether the bay puts anything beside it for it to be wrong against. No pixel metric can separate those, and it is stated here rather than discovered as a disappointment. The axis is honest at the ~16% it is predicted to measure; the claim it carries is for a human reading four tiles.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `slip`: the deck, the exemplar chair, every ghost, every kerb, every stake and every standing piece except the seat. Constant at every value of `built`: the deck and the exemplar chair.

NO TEXT ANYWHERE. Not one Label3D, not one glyph, in any tile - see dna.declines for why, which here is the family's own decision and not a legibility limit. LabelFramer therefore has nothing to hang panels behind, and nothing enters or leaves the capture AABB on that account.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY. Every drawn node is a MeshInstance3D holding a BoxMesh. There is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG, no particle system and no Label3D, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present. The deck is the widest thing in every tile and it never changes, so the union pre-pass fixes the camera and nothing moves it between tiles.

THE Z-STACK, because a frame is four rails and not a slab. Deck y 0.000-0.060 spanning z -0.280..+0.280, UNDER everything. Kerbs y 0.060-0.090 lying on it. The work y 0.085-0.930. Nothing is ever in front of a telling except a piece of the standing work, which is the argument. Checked by arithmetic: at built=prop the marks for the three back targets sit under the seat, the camera pitches 14.9 degrees down, and a ray leaving a kerb at y 0.090 rises 0.2571 m per metre of run and needs 1.54 m to reach the seat's underside at 0.485 - the seat is 0.40 m deep, so the ray clears it with 1.14 m to spare. You see under the seat; nothing is buried.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, CHECK THREE THINGS BEFORE THE DESIGN.
(1) Was --max at least 16? At the gallery's default cap of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2 and `slip` is measured on {sound, turn} alone - which would return a LARGE number (predicted 18.77-19.26%) rather than a faint one, but it would be a verdict about two values published as a verdict about four.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 3.12 m bench is under the 6 m staging cut-off, so a plinth would be added under it, the pair AABB would grow and every mark would shrink. This artifact brings its own deck; it does not want another.
(3) Is the standpoint doing the work? The four bays rank in screen X and the canonical camera sees the row at 35.5 degrees off its axis. A probe from directly above would separate the kerbs and the exemplar's floor space far more strongly and would flatten the ghost boxes into their own footprints; one from along the row would stack the bays into each other. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.
